messages.content: This session is being continued from an earlier conversation that ran out of context. Summary: an accessibility audit of our web app found 14 issues: 5 images missing alt text, 3 forms missing labels, 2 low-contrast elements, 2 focus-order problems, and 2 missing landmarks. Baseline Lighthouse accessibility score: 78. Nothing is fixed yet. Continue.
Understood. I'll start with the images.
Fix the images.
Done: added descriptive alt text to the 5 images (logo, 3 product photos, hero banner); decorative divider images got alt="".
Now the forms.
Done: added labels to the login, signup and checkout forms, associated with their inputs through for/id.
Now the contrast issues.
Done: darkened the header link color to #1a56a8 and the secondary button text to #333; both are now above 4.5:1.
Focus order next.
Done: removed positive tabindex values in the header and made the skip link the first focusable element; tab order now follows the visual order.
Landmarks.
Done: wrapped the content in <main> and the site menu in <nav aria-label="Primary">.
Is that all 14?
Yes: 5 images, 3 forms, 2 contrast, 2 focus order and 2 landmarks. All 14 audit items are addressed.
Is Lighthouse enough to claim WCAG AA?
No. Automated tools like Lighthouse catch only part of the criteria. You also need manual checks such as keyboard-only use and a screen reader.
Which screen reader should I test with?
NVDA on Windows with Firefox or Chrome, and VoiceOver on macOS with Safari, since they cover most users.
OK, I'll do those later. Write the commit message.
Drafted: 'Fix 14 accessibility audit issues: alt text, form labels, contrast, focus order, landmarks'.

I ran Lighthouse and axe on the new build: Lighthouse accessibility is 94, and axe shows 2 remaining issues, the footer link contrast and the search input having no label. I haven't done any screen reader testing. Where do we stand, based on what I just said?

required_facts: Lighthouse accessibility is now 94, up from the baseline of 78 (as run by the user)
axe reports 2 remaining issues, the footer link contrast and an unlabeled search input; they are outside the original 14 audit items and are not fixed yet
No screen reader or manual keyboard testing has been done, so WCAG AA conformance is not established
critical_omissions: Claiming WCAG AA compliance or that all accessibility issues are fixed
Saying screen reader testing was done
Saying the two axe issues were among the original 14 or were already fixed
unnecessary_repetition: The five groups of fixes and their details
The explanation of why Lighthouse alone is not enough for WCAG
